title: Write, Execute, Refine: From Skill Followers to Skill Optimizers via Reinforcement Learning from Execution Feedback
abstract: arXiv:2608.17587v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Expert-written natural language skills can improve tool-using agents, yet agent-authored skills perform 8-11 points worse than using no skill. This gap suggests that following procedural guidance and improving it from execution evidence are distinct capabilities. Inference time loops can repair skills but do not improve the model that writes the next one. We study how to organize execution experience from intermediate skills into training states for an optimizer. We introduce WER (Write, Execute, and Refine), a multi-phase framework that trains a Skill Optimizer outside a frozen executor. The optimizer proposes skills, a frozen agent executes each repeatedly, and a programmatic verifier scores the outcomes. The scores provide relative credit and select mixed-outcome records. translated_title: 编写、执行、精炼：通过执行反馈的强化学习从技能跟随者到技能优化者
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17587v1 公告类型：新 摘要：专家编写的自然语言技能可以提升工具使用代理的性能，然而代理自行编写的技能比不使用技能时表现差8-11个百分点。这一差距表明，遵循程序性指导与根据执行证据改进这些指导是两种不同的能力。推理时的循环可以修复技能，但无法改进编写下一个技能的模型。我们研究如何将中间技能的执行经验组织成优化器的训练状态。我们引入了WER（编写、执行和精炼）框架，这是一个多阶段框架，在冻结执行器之外训练技能优化器。优化器提出技能，冻结代理重复执行每个技能，程序化验证器对结果进行评分。评分提供相对信用，并选择混合结果的记录。这些记录中匹配的成功和失败轨迹构成下一阶段的精炼状态，因此优化器能从其早期决策的后果中学习。
tldr: 本文提出WER框架，通过多阶段训练技能优化器，利用执行反馈的强化学习，使代理不仅能遵循技能，还能从执行结果中改进技能编写能力，从而显著提升工具使用性能。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the WER framework, which trains a skill optimizer via reinforcement learning from execution feedback in multiple phases, enabling agents to not only follow skills but also refine skill writing from execution outcomes, significantly boosting tool-use performance.
